'''Spinach soup''' is a [[soup]] prepared using [[spinach]] as a primary ingredient.<ref name="Spitler Yoakam 2015"/> A common dish around the world, the soup can be prepared as a [[broth]]-based or cream-based soup, and the latter can be referred to as "cream of spinach soup."<ref name="Briggs 2008"/><ref name="St. Louis Post-Dispatch 2016"/> In [[China]], a spinach and tofu soup is also known as "emerald and white jade soup"; spinach and tofu represent [[emerald]] and [[Nephrite|white jade]] respectively,<ref>{{cite book |author1=Deh-Ta Hsiung |author2=Nina Simonds |title=The Food of China |date=2001 |publisher=bay books |location=London |isbn=9780681025844 |page=60}}</ref> and thus the spinach soup itself can be called "emerald soup".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Parkinson |first1=Rhpnda |title=The Everything Chinese Cookbook |date=2003 |publisher=Adams Media |location=Avon, MA |isbn=9781580629546 |page=[https://archive.org/details/everythingchines00laur/page/63 63] |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/everythingchines00laur/page/63 }}</ref> Fresh, canned or frozen spinach can be used, and the spinach can be used whole, [[purée]]d or chopped.<ref name="Spitler Yoakam 2015"/><ref name="Parker-Pope 2016"/><ref name="Stock 2014"/> Additional ingredients can include onion, green onion, carrot, celery, tomatoes, potatoes, lemon juice, olive oil, seasonings, salt and pepper.<ref name="St. Louis Post-Dispatch 2016"/><ref name="Stock 2014"/><ref name="Agarwal 2014"/><ref name="Kamal 2011"/> Spinach soup is typically served hot, but can also be served as a cold soup.<ref name="Child 2012"/><ref name="Molokhovets Toomre 1998"/> Prior to being served, it can be topped or garnished with ingredients such as sour cream and [[crème fraîche]].<ref name="Chase 1959"/><ref name="Soup 2009"/>
